```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab10", title = "Time series regression 2")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Relative likelihood of a model with Delta AICc = 6 is about:",
  q2 = "Two independent random walks regressed on each other often show:",
  q3 = "A scenario forecast needs:",
  q4 = "In one sentence, why is a significant slope not enough to claim causation?"
)
```

## What you will do

Relative likelihood and the spurious-regression warning.

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `fpp3`, `learnr`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("0.05", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.0025"),
  answer("6"),
  answer("1"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("A spurious significant slope", correct = TRUE),
  answer("White-noise residuals and a slope of zero"),
  answer("An airline model"),
  answer("No fitted line"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("A future path for the regressor", correct = TRUE),
  answer("Only the historical y"),
  answer("A Prophet holiday"),
  answer("d=2 always"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```
```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "Shared trend / unit roots can create a significant slope.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
